infoPages.title: Dragon Medical One Security & Australian Data Residency
infoPages.metaDescription: Where Dragon Medical One stores audio and text, what's encrypted, what isn't, and what Australian data residency actually means in practice.
infoPages.heroHeading: How secure is Dragon Medical One, and where is the data stored?
infoPages.lede: Dragon Medical One runs on Microsoft Azure. Subscriptions sold by Voice Recognition Australia are provisioned on the Australian Azure tenant, so audio and transcribed text are processed in Australia, not overseas. This page covers the specifics: which encryption standards, which certifications apply, what is and isn't stored, and the questions an IT or compliance team will want answered before a deployment.
infoPages.tldr: Dragon Medical One is hosted on Microsoft Azure with Australian-region processing for AU subscriptions. Audio is streamed for recognition and is not retained on the client device. Traffic is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2, AES-256) and at rest. The underlying Azure platform is HITRUST CSF certified and ISO 27001 certified. Voice Recognition Australia handles enrolment, configuration, and ongoing support locally.

sections.heading: Where Dragon Medical One processes audio for Australian customers
paragraphs: Dragon Medical One is a cloud service. The desktop app on the clinician's PC captures audio and streams it to Nuance/Microsoft servers, which perform recognition and stream text back. For subscriptions sold by Voice Recognition Australia, the service is provisioned on the Australian Azure tenant, with two geographically distributed Azure regions in Australia for resilience.

The implication for an Australian healthcare buyer: audio recognition happens inside Australia, not the US or EU. That matters for Privacy Act compliance, hospital procurement, and conversations with information security officers who ask where does the data go?

sections.heading: What's stored, what isn't

specTable.label: Audio recordings
specTable.value: Streamed for recognition. Not retained on the client device. Refer to current Microsoft/Nuance documentation for retention policies on the cloud side.

specTable.label: Transcribed text
specTable.value: Written to whichever clinical application the clinician was dictating into (Best Practice, Genie, Medical Director, Shexie, Gentu, etc.). Not stored in Dragon Medical One as a clinical record.

specTable.label: User profile
specTable.value: Stored in the cloud, linked to the clinician's account. Includes personal vocabulary additions, AutoText shortcuts, and custom voice commands.

specTable.label: Specialty vocabulary
specTable.value: Selected at login (general practice, cardiology, oncology, radiology, etc.). Loaded from Microsoft/Nuance vocabulary set.

specTable.label: Usage analytics
specTable.value: Aggregate usage data available to system administrators via the Nuance Management Center for hospital/enterprise deployments.

sections.note: Verify current retention and data handling specifics directly with Voice Recognition Australia or in your tenancy contract. Cloud product details can change without notice.

sections.heading: Encryption and certifications
paragraphs: Three security claims are documented by Microsoft for the Azure infrastructure Dragon Medical One runs on:
list: Encryption at rest: AES-256 on Azure storage.
Infrastructure certifications: HITRUST CSF certified, ISO 27001 certified, Azure compliance posture (GDPR, SOC 2 Type II) on the underlying platform.
sections.note: Certifications listed apply to the Azure platform Dragon Medical One is deployed on. They are public Microsoft/Nuance claims. Healthcare buyers should request current compliance documentation from Microsoft or Voice Recognition Australia as part of procurement.

sections.heading: How this compares to other dictation options
paragraphs: Australian healthcare buyers comparing options usually look at three security postures:

specTable.label: Dragon Medical One
specTable.value: Cloud, Australian Azure tenant for AU subscriptions, encrypted in transit and at rest, HITRUST CSF / ISO 27001 on Azure infrastructure.

specTable.label: Dragon Professional 16 (desktop)
specTable.value: Fully local on the clinician's Windows PC. Audio and text never leave the machine. Best for environments that mandate offline-only processing. No medical vocabulary built in.

specTable.label: Windows / M365 Dictation
specTable.value: Cloud, processed in the Microsoft 365 tenant your organisation is subscribed to. Tenancy region depends on M365 setup. General vocabulary only - no medical specialties.

specTable.label: AI scribe tools (Heidi, Lyrebird, etc.)
specTable.value: Cloud, vendor-specific data handling. Generative AI means output is not a verbatim record of what was said. Different regulatory considerations apply. See Dragon Medical One vs AI scribes.

sections.heading: Questions an IT or compliance team will ask
paragraphs: If you're putting Dragon Medical One in front of a hospital infosec review or a practice manager evaluating procurement, expect questions like the ones below. We'll walk you through the answers and provide written documentation for procurement files where needed.
list: Where is the user profile stored?
What happens to the audio after recognition?
Which encryption standards apply in transit and at rest?
Which compliance certifications apply to the underlying infrastructure?
Is there a contractual data processing agreement available?
How are user accounts provisioned and deprovisioned?
Does Dragon Medical One create a patient record or feed into one?
What's the disaster recovery posture between the two Australian Azure regions?

faqs.q: Is Dragon Medical One hosted in Australia?
faqs.a: Yes. Subscriptions sold by Voice Recognition Australia are provisioned on the Australian Microsoft Azure tenant, with two geographically distributed Australian Azure regions providing resilience. Audio is processed in Australia, not the US or EU.

HIPAA is a US regulation and does not apply directly in Australia. In the US, Dragon Medical One is positioned by Microsoft as HIPAA-aligned. For Australian healthcare buyers, the relevant frameworks are the Privacy Act 1988, Australian Privacy Principles, and any state-specific health-records legislation. The underlying Azure platform is HITRUST CSF certified and ISO 27001 certified, which Australian compliance teams typically accept as evidence of mature security controls. Discuss specific compliance requirements with your privacy or compliance officer during evaluation.

faqs.q: Is the audio recording stored after Dragon Medical One transcribes it?
faqs.a: The audio is streamed to the cloud for recognition processing and is not retained on the client device. Server-side retention is governed by current Microsoft/Nuance policies, which can change. Request current data handling specifics in writing as part of your procurement process if this matters for your compliance posture.

faqs.q: What encryption does Dragon Medical One use?
faqs.a: Traffic between the client and the cloud uses TLS 1.2 with AES-256. Data at rest on Azure storage uses AES-256. These are the encryption standards Microsoft documents for Azure healthcare workloads.

faqs.q: Can our hospital IT team manage Dragon Medical One centrally?
faqs.a: Yes. The Nuance Management Center (NMC) gives hospital IT teams a single console to manage user accounts, speech profiles, shared AutoText, shared vocabulary, and usage analytics across the organisation. Voice Recognition Australia configures NMC as part of enterprise deployments.

faqs.q: How does this compare to keeping dictation offline with Dragon Professional 16?
faqs.a: Dragon Professional 16 processes everything locally on the clinician's Windows PC, so audio and text never leave the machine. It works fully offline after activation. The trade-off is that it has no medical specialty vocabularies, no PowerMic Mobile, no centralised management, and no automatic updates. If offline-only processing is a contractual or compliance requirement, Dragon Professional 16 is the right choice; if not, Dragon Medical One is built for clinical work and the security posture is appropriate for most Australian healthcare environments.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about a security review?
faqs.a: Contact Voice Recognition Australia. We provide current Microsoft and Nuance compliance documentation, can arrange direct contact with Microsoft healthcare cloud specialists for hospital-scale deployments, and can answer practical implementation questions about your specific environment.

faqs.q: How much does Dragon Medical One cost in Australia?
faqs.a: Contact us for current pricing. Dragon Medical One is sold as an annual subscription that includes the software licence, PowerMic Mobile app, remote installation, personalised training, and 12 months of Australian technical support. Enterprise and volume pricing is available for hospitals and large practices.

faqs.q: Does Dragon Medical One work with Best Practice, Genie, and Medical Director?
faqs.a: Yes. Dragon Medical One works with Best Practice, Genie Solutions, Medical Director, Shexie, Gentu, and many other clinical software systems. It floats over your existing application and dictates into any text field. We also support Epic and Cerner for hospital environments.

faqs.q: Do I need to train Dragon Medical One to recognise my voice?
faqs.a: No significant voice training is required. Dragon Medical One uses cloud-based artificial intelligence to automatically adapt to your accent and dictation style over time. You select your medical specialty when you first log in and can start dictating immediately.

Dragon Medical One for Australian customers runs on Microsoft Azure with data residency across two geographically distributed locations within Australia. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Audio is streamed for recognition processing and is not stored on the client device.

faqs.q: What is Dragon Copilot and is it available in Australia?
faqs.a: Dragon Copilot is Microsoft's newer ambient AI assistant that combines Dragon Medical One dictation with ambient listening and generative AI to create structured clinical notes from consultations. As of March 2026, Dragon Copilot is available in the US, UK, Canada, and parts of Europe. It is not yet publicly listed as available in Australia. We expect Australian availability in due course. Register your interest on our Dragon Copilot page.

faqs.q: How is Dragon Medical One different from AI scribes?
faqs.a: Dragon Medical One produces verbatim transcription - exactly what you say appears in your clinical notes. AI scribes listen to consultations and generate summarised or restructured notes using generative AI. This means AI scribe output is not a verbatim record and may introduce clinical documentation risks. The TGA may also have implications for AI tools that generate clinical content. Dragon Medical One gives you direct control over what appears in the patient record.

faqs.q: Can I use my mobile phone as a microphone?
faqs.a: Yes. The PowerMic Mobile app is included with every Dragon Medical One subscription. It turns your iPhone or Android phone into a secure wireless microphone. You can move between consulting rooms and computers without carrying separate hardware.

faqs.q: What happens if I have technical issues?
faqs.a: Every Dragon Medical One subscription from Voice Recognition Australia includes 12 months of Australian-based technical support. Our team can remotely connect to your system to troubleshoot and resolve issues. We also provide access to subscriber-only training videos.
